title: Find the Maximum Number of Elements in Subset
summary: Given an array of positive integers, find the largest subset that can be arranged in a specific pattern: starting with a number, followed by its squares, fourth powers, and so on, then back down to the original number.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, find the largest subset that can be arranged in a specific pattern: starting with a number, followed by its squares, fourth powers, and so on, then back down to the original number. For example, a valid subset could be [2, 4, 16, 4, 2] or [3, 9, 3]. The task is to return the maximum size of such a subset.
constraints: nums contains at least two positive integers.
Choose an odd-length multiset arrangeable symmetrically as x,x²,x⁴,...,peak,...,x⁴,x²,x.
Return the greatest possible selected length; duplicate copies are required on both sides of every non-peak level.
hints: Every non-peak chain value needs two copies, while the final peak needs one; value one is a special fixed point.
Count values and try each non-one value as a base, repeatedly squaring while two copies exist.
Add two per paired level, then add one for an existing peak or remove the last pair if no peak exists; use the largest odd count of ones.
A base uniquely determines all later powers, so the count walk finds its longest feasible symmetric chain and checking every base is exhaustive.
editorial: A base uniquely determines all later powers, so the count walk finds its longest feasible symmetric chain and checking every base is exhaustive.

tests.explanation: Two copies of two with one four form the valid arrangement [2,4,2] of length three.
No nontrivial chain has duplicate endpoints and only one 1 may be used for odd length, so the answer is one.
